OSCT docs

API

Content model reference

What an experience is made of, content schema 6.2: every built-in type with its parameters, their ranges and defaults. It is what the tool describe_content_model answers an agent, and what the editor's rows are built from.

The experience

ExperienceData: { id, title, passes?, environment?, appearance?, book?, recognition? } – the experience, the top level of the content (content schema 4.0). book = BookData { author, publisher? }: the printed book it accompanies, print data only; none = not a book (a wall, a room, an exhibition). update_experience changes the title (the reader's splash, home page and account show it) and the printed book – its author and publisher (the splash shows them), book: null removes it. recognition (content schema 4.2): "original" (none = the default: the reader makes every target's recognition data from its printed image) or "prepared" (a target's frame made ahead where it has one) – update_experience recognition. Every experience adds, moves and removes its scenes in the editor.

Scenes, surfaces and groups

Content schema 3.0: the configuration holds scenes (in order – their position is the experience's order, nothing numbers them), initialScene (the scene the reader starts on – it cannot be removed) and groups ([{ id, label }]). SceneData: { id, label, group?, surfaces, passes? } – id stable and invisible (links /scene/<id>, progress, entries name it); label = what the reader's switcher and lists show (186–187, Cover, Studio wall), free text; group = the id of one of the experience's groups (one stop of the reader's bottom switcher); passes = the scene's own post-processing. SurfaceData: { id, label?, widthMm, heightMm, place } – one physical area of the scene: a double page is one surface (twice the page's width), a cover one, a wall or a poster one; surfaces are free areas next to each other – no left / right, no front / back; label = what is printed on it, free text. place: { x, y, z, rx, ry, rz } – the surface's centre in the scene's one coordinate system: mm, the origin on the table at the middle of the scene's first row of surfaces (a double page: its spine), +x right, +y up, +z towards the reader; rx, ry, rz in degrees (Euler XYZ). Unrotated a surface lies flat, face up, its top edge away from the reader – a page on the table; a wall ahead stands up: rx 90. Tools: list_scenes reads them (with each surface's editor-only reference image), get_scene one with its entries, add_scene adds one anywhere from a preset, put_scene changes label, group, surfaces (the whole list – a surface without a place is laid in a row) and passes, put_surface changes, adds, moves or removes one surface alone, move_scenes moves one or several (or into / out of a group), delete_scene removes one with everything on it (two steps); group_scenes / rename_group / ungroup handle groups; set_surface_reference sets a surface's reference image (never content).

presetsdouble · single · wall
placeKeysx · y · z · rx · ry · rz
surfacesMax32
referenceFitscover · contain · stretch

An entry

An entry is top level: { id, category, title, scene, surface?, body, author?, image?, imageLevels?, caption?, media?, tags, target? } – scene = the id of its scene (required: where the reader finds it), surface = one of that scene's surfaces (only when the scene has several). add_entry makes one, with its target or without (read only in the list); get_entries reads every field; update_entry changes them (scene moves it, surface null takes it off a surface; image: a Library picture, imageLevels (content schema 4.3): the same picture at 512 / 1024 / 2048 px longest side – [{ level, src }], the reader's media quality chooses one; caption: the line under it in plain text, media: a link's http(s) URL).

categoriesglossary · video · text · link

An entry's text

An entry's body (content schema 2.23) is Markdown with the experience's variables, rendered alike by the reader and the editor's preview. Markdown, only this much: a blank line starts a paragraph, a single line break stays one, *emphasis* or _emphasis_, **strong** or __strong__, [link text](https://…) (http, https and mailto – any other link stays text), a backslash escapes (\* is a star). No headings, lists, images, code or HTML – HTML shows as text. Variables (the syntax of SCUTOONS' message boxes, ink's inline syntax): {hasKey} prints a variable – a bare camelCase name of the behaviour variables and the plugins' api.vars, read from the innermost scope that has it (scene, stage, session, experience); {tries > 2: Try the window.} and {hasKey: The door opens.|It is locked.} choose a text; expressions have numbers, "texts", true / false, and or not, == != < <= > >=, + - * / mod and parentheses. A variable that is not set shows as nothing and is false – so {name: {name}|friend} is a fallback. \{ \} \| write the characters. No lists ({a|b}) and no functions: they render nothing and update_entry refuses them. An older reader shows the source as written.

exampleHello {name: **{name}**|stranger}. {hasKey: The door opens.|The door is *locked*.} See [the map](https://example.org/map).

A target

TargetData: { id, imageSrc, entity?: EntityData | { ref }, place?, enabled?, recognition?, recognitionOff? }. imageSrc = the printed image (an uploaded image asset's url). enabled: false switches the target off – the reader leaves it and its entry out until it is switched on, the editor keeps both; leave it out for a target in the experience. recognition (content schema 4.1) = the image tracker's grey frame made ahead from imageSrc by osct targets prepare or the editor – not written here; the API drops it when imageSrc changes. The reader uses it only when the experience's recognition is "prepared" and the target has no recognitionOff: true (content schema 4.2, put_target recognitionOff).

place

Where the target lies (TargetPlace, content schema 3.0): { surface?, x, y, width, height? } – its box in mm from the top left corner of a surface of its entry's scene; surface = the surface's id, required when the scene has several. The editor's stage lays the target there; the reader does not need it. put_target place, add_entry target.place; null removes it.

example

{
  "surface": "surface",
  "x": 40,
  "y": 60,
  "width": 80
}

An entity: the node tree

An AR entity is a tree of nodes (EntityData): { id?, name?, type, assets, params?, filters?, components?, material?, children?, text?, color? }. The root sits on the target (1 unit = the target image's width, origin in its centre); every node's params place it relative to its parent. At most 8 levels. Shared entities live under a ref and are used by targets as { ref }.

namename (content schema 2.12, optional): what the editor's tree shows instead of the type – give the nodes of a larger tree names ("door", "hint") so the person finds them; the reader ignores it.
nodeTypesgroup · model · video · image · text · light
texttext nodes: text (the line; {{entry.title}} and {{experience.title}} are replaced) and color (#rrggbb, default white).

assets

The node's own files: [{ id, assetType, src, textures?, levels? }] – empty for group and text. src is an absolute URL (an uploaded asset's url) or a /assets/content/… path of the imported content.

assetTypesglb · gltf · video · image · audio
texturestextures (content schema 2.27, optional, a model file only): the model's colour map in several sizes – [{ material?, sizes: [{ size, src }] }], size one of 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 (px, a square picture), each once, smallest first. The model file carries the smallest map and shows with it at once; the reader's texture quality chooses the size that is loaded, so the mesh loads once. material = the glTF material whose map the set is; none = every material of the model (a model baked into one map). Upload each size as an image (upload_asset tells its width) and put its url into src.
levelslevels (content schema 4.3, #331, optional, an image, video or audio file only): the medium in several qualities – [{ level, src }], each level once, smallest first; level = an image's longest side (512 / 1024 / 2048 px), a video's height (480 / 720 / 1080), a sound's bitrate (64 / 128 / 192 kbps). The reader's media quality (Info → Settings: auto / low / medium / high) chooses the level it loads, falling back to the nearest; src stays the file an older reader loads – put the middle level there. Video levels are made before the upload (the editor never encodes video); upload each level (upload_asset) and put its url into src. Set them with put_entity / put_target (the node's assets).

pluginNodeTypes

A plugin's node type (content schema 2.13, api.registerNodeType): written as type: <its name>, its parameters in params next to the placement; src only when its spec says which file (none | glb | video | image). The API refuses a type no plugin of the experience registers when the plugins recorded what they register (schema 2.14).

Placement

entity.params: position [x, y, z] in target widths (x → right, y → the top of the target image, z → out of the surface), rotation [x, y, z] in degrees (Euler XYZ), scale as one number or [x, y, z]. Missing values take the type's defaults.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
position-1 … 1 · in target widths · step 0.01x → right, y → top of the page, z → out of the page
rotation-180 … 180 · in ° · step 1Degrees, Euler order XYZ (three.js uses radians)
scale0.05 … 3 · in × · step 0.01Relative to the target's width

Components

entity.components: [{ type, …params }] – the built-in types, and the components and material layers a plugin registers (used the same way).

typePattern^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]{0,39}$

animation builtIn

Plays one of the model's animation clips (glTF). Without this component every clip plays in a loop.

nodeTypesmodel
ParameterKindDefaultWhat
clipstring""The clip's name – empty plays the first clip. (shown as “clip”)
playOnchoice · "found" | "tap" | "never""found"When the clip starts: when the page is found, when the entity is tapped, or never (the editor's timeline only). (shown as “plays on”)
stopOnchoice · "lost" | "never""lost"When it stops: when the page is lost, or never (it keeps its time while the page is away). (shown as “stops on”)
loopbooleantrueRepeat the clip; off = play it once and hold the last frame. (shown as “loop”)
speednumber · 0.1 … 4 · in × · step 0.11Playback speed. (shown as “speed”)

reveal builtIn

How this entity appears the first time its target is found (the entry is unlocked with it): a look – built in or a plugin's – with its parameters, in place of the experience's. On any node: its subtree animates with it.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
lookstring""The look this entity appears with – a built-in one (inflateDissolve, printLift, fade) or a plugin's – in place of the experience's. Empty = the experience's. The look's own parameters follow. (shown as “look”)

found builtIn

How this entity appears every time its target is found after the first (and the first too, while it has no reveal): a look with its parameters, in place of the experience's. On any node: its subtree animates with it.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
lookstring""The look this entity appears with – a built-in one (inflateDissolve, printLift, fade) or a plugin's – in place of the experience's. Empty = the experience's. The look's own parameters follow. (shown as “look”)

lost builtIn

How this entity disappears when its target is lost: a look with its parameters – it plays rewound, in the look's disappear time – in place of the experience's. On any node: its subtree animates with it.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
lookstring""The look this entity appears with – a built-in one (inflateDissolve, printLift, fade) or a plugin's – in place of the experience's. Empty = the experience's. The look's own parameters follow. (shown as “look”)

behaviour builtIn

Rules without code: on an event (found, lost, tap, unlocked or a named event), when variables match, do actions – play, pause or stop a clip, show or hide a node, set a variable, emit an event.

moments

An entity's own look for a moment (content schema 2.30): the built-in components reveal (the first find of a target), found (every later find) and lost (the target is lost) on a node of the entity – any node – { type: reveal, look: printLift, duration: 900 }. look = a look's type – a built-in one (appearance.builtIn) or one a plugin of the experience registers (api.registerAppearance, appearance.plugins) – and "" or no look = the experience's; the other keys are the look's parameters (appearance.builtIn[look].params), only the values that differ from its defaults. Changing the look means writing the component anew with its parameters. They win over the experience's appearance: the root node's moment, else its found (for reveal and lost), else the experience's moment, the experience's found, the default. A node with a look of its own animates its subtree apart from the rest, with that look (a child's moment: its own, else its found, else it is part of its parent's); the root plays the experience's look where it names none.

typesreveal · found · lost

example

[
  {
    "type": "reveal",
    "look": "printLift",
    "duration": 900
  },
  {
    "type": "lost",
    "look": "fade",
    "outDuration": 250
  }
]

behaviour

The built-in behaviour (content schema 2.19, any node type): rules without code – { type: behaviour, rules: [{ on, when?, do }] }. The same grammar holds a scene's and the experience's rules (logic, content schema 5.0). on = the node's own event or any other camelCase name, an event of the stage's bus (a scene event a plugin or a behaviour emits, or a core event). when = an expression (content schema 5.0 – the object form { variable: value } is gone): the language of the entries' {…} texts without braces – camelCase variable names, numbers, "texts", true / false, and or not && || !, == != < <= > >=, + - * / mod, parentheses – e.g. hasKey && tries > 2, mood == "calm" || !doorOpen. The rule runs when the value is true (0, "", false and a variable that is not set are false); no functions, no dotted names. do = one action or a list, run in order: play: <clip> ("" = the node's own clip – its animation component's, else the first) with optional node: <name>; pause / stop / show / hide: <node name> ("" = the behaviour's own node; a node of its subtree by its name); set: { variable: value } with optional scope (the variable's declared scope, else scene; stage, session, or experience – the whole experience; null deletes) – a value is an expression (content schema 5.0): tries + 1, hasKey, "calm" (a text is the language's text literal, in YAML '"calm"'; a number or true / false may stand bare); emit: <event> (a scene event, never a core event); goto: scene:<id> (content schema 5.0) – the reader opens that scene, as a link to /scene/<id>. A string runs a verb on the own node: play, pause, stop, show, hide. On one event every rule's condition is read first, then the matching rules run in their order. Variables are read like a plugin's api.vars.get (the innermost scope that has it).

nodeEventsfound · lost · tap · unlocked
coreEventstargetFound · targetLost · targetUnlocked · targetTapped · sceneChanged · arState · varChanged
actionsplay · pause · stop · show · hide · set · emit · goto
scopesscene · stage · session · experience

example

{
  "type": "behaviour",
  "rules": [
    {
      "on": "tap",
      "do": [
        {
          "play": "rattle"
        },
        {
          "set": {
            "hasKey": true
          },
          "scope": "experience"
        },
        {
          "emit": "keyRattled"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "on": "found",
      "when": "hasKey && tries > 2",
      "do": [
        {
          "hide": "hint"
        },
        {
          "emit": "openDoor"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "on": "tap",
      "when": "doorOpen",
      "do": {
        "goto": "scene:epilogue"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Rules of a scene and of the experience

A scene's and the experience's rules (content schema 5.0): logic = { rules: [{ on, when?, do }], canvas? } on a scene (live while the scene is open – put_scene logic) and on the experience (live for the whole session, across scene switches – the editor's Logic view, PUT /editor/experiences/{id}/logic). The rules are the behaviour's grammar (components.behaviour) with three differences: on listens to the bus only – a scene event or a core event (coreEvents), never a node's own found / lost / tap / unlocked (use targetFound / targetTapped); show / hide / pause / stop and play's node name a node by address target:<targetId>/<node name> (target:<targetId> alone = the entity's root; a scene's rules only its own targets); no shorthand strings. goto: scene:<id> works in every rule (a node's too): the reader opens that scene. sceneChanged reaches a scene's and the experience's rules once the new scene's nodes are built. canvas = the editor's Logic view's own data – { groups?: [{ id, label, members: [node ids] }], notes?: [{ id, text, x, y, author?, box?, view? }] (schema 5.3: a note with box stands beside that box – x, y its offset; view = the target view of a scene canvas it shows in), folds?: [node ids], exposed?: { <box id>: [port ids] } (schema 5.1: the ports shown on a box beyond its wired ones), positions?: { <box id>: { x, y } } (schema 5.2: boxes pinned over the layout); a group may carry colour (#rrggbb) and folded (schema 5.2) } – stored and exported, never published to readers; leave it to the editor.

variablesTyped variables (content schema 5.0): experience.variables = { name: { type, scope?, default? } } (PUT /editor/experiences/{id}/variables) – type number | integer | boolean | string; a variable not declared takes the type of its first set. A set of another type, a comparison of different types and a when that is not true / false are problems; && || ! need true / false, - * / % < > need numbers, + adds numbers or joins texts (never both); an integer goes where a number is wanted, nothing else converts. The reader refuses a value of the wrong type (also a plugin's api.vars.set) and keeps the old one; a declared variable not set reads as its default.
variableTypesnumber · integer · boolean · string
coreEventstargetFound · targetLost · targetUnlocked · targetTapped · sceneChanged · arState · varChanged

addresses

gotoscene:<sceneId>
nodetarget:<targetId>/<node name>

example

{
  "rules": [
    {
      "on": "doorOpened",
      "when": "hasKey",
      "do": [
        {
          "show": "target:door/hint"
        },
        {
          "play": "creak",
          "node": "target:door"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "on": "targetUnlocked",
      "when": "unlocks >= 3",
      "do": [
        {
          "set": {
            "chapterDone": true,
            "unlocks": "unlocks + 1"
          },
          "scope": "experience"
        },
        {
          "goto": "scene:epilogue"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Filters

entity.filters (video nodes only): [{ type, …params }], applied in order.

chromaKey types

Makes one color of the video transparent – a colored background (neon green is safest) or pure black/white.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
colorcolor"#00ff00"Key color (#rrggbb) that becomes transparent. (shown as “key color”)
modechoice · "auto" | "chroma" | "luma""auto"chroma compares the color tone (for green, purple, …), luma the brightness (for black, white). auto: luma for neutral colors (black, grey, white), chroma otherwise. (shown as “compare by”)
thresholdnumber · 0 … 10.3How close to the key color a pixel must be to disappear. Higher = more is removed. (shown as “threshold”)
softnessnumber · 0.001 … 10.08Width of the soft edge between transparent and visible. Higher = softer, more see-through edges. (shown as “soft edge”)
spillnumber · 0.001 … 10.1Removes the key color's tint on edges (chroma only). Higher = more grey on edges. (shown as “spill”)
opacitynumber · 0 … 11Opacity of the whole video after keying. 1 = fully visible. (shown as “opacity”)

Materials

entity.material (content schema 2.17, plugin API 1.4): { type, params? } – a material a plugin registers (api.registerMaterial) replaces the material of the node's meshes (a model, an image or video plane, a plugin node); its layers still add on top. Every material is a plugin's: the API refuses one no plugin of the experience registers when the plugins recorded what they register, the publish refuses one no compiled plugin provides (409 unknown-materials).

texturesA parameter of kind texture takes "" (none), a procedural texture's type (api.registerTexture – e.g. "caustics"), { type, …parameters } for one with other values, or a file: an uploaded image or video asset's url, or a /assets/content/… path.
typePattern^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]{0,39}$

Post-processing passes

Post-processing over the whole rendered AR image: [{ type, enabled?, …params }], run in order. The experience's passes (put_experience_passes) are the master every scene shows; a scene's own (put_scene passes) replace them for that scene, [] turns them off there, null gives the scene the experience's again. enabled: false (content schema 2.22) switches one pass off – it keeps its place and values, the chain skips it, it does not count towards the phone budget; leave enabled out for a pass that runs. A 2.21 reader ignores it and runs the pass. The built-in types, and (content schema 2.21) a pass a plugin of the experience registers (api.registerPass) – written the same way, its parameters checked against the recorded spec. A pass no compiled plugin provides is refused by the publish (409 unknown-passes); a 2.20 reader refuses an experience that names one. Up to three passes and one bloom per list fit the phone budget.

bloom builtIn

Bright parts of the image glow – blurred and added back as light over everything, the camera picture included.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
strengthnumber · 0 … 3 · step 0.051How much light the glow adds.
radiusnumber · 0 … 1 · step 0.050.4How far the glow spreads.
thresholdnumber · 0 … 1 · step 0.010.85Brightness from which a pixel glows (1 = only brighter than white).

vignette builtIn

The edges of the picture fade to a colour (black by default) – the AR layer and the camera picture alike.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
strengthnumber · 0 … 1 · step 0.010.6How dark the edges get (1 = fully the colour).
radiusnumber · 0 … 1.5 · step 0.010.6Distance from the centre where the fade begins (1 = the sides).
softnessnumber · 0.01 … 1.5 · step 0.010.6How wide the fade is.
colorcolor"#000000"The colour the edges fade to.

grade builtIn

Colour grading – exposure, contrast, saturation and a tint. Of the AR layer alone, or of the whole picture with the camera picture.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
reachchoice · "ar" | "all""ar"What is graded: ar = the AR layer alone (the camera picture keeps its colours), all = the whole picture, the camera picture included.
exposurenumber · -2 … 2 · in EV · step 0.050Brighter (+) or darker (−) in stops.
contrastnumber · 0 … 2 · step 0.0511 = as rendered, 0 = flat grey, 2 = hard.
saturationnumber · 0 … 2 · step 0.0511 = as rendered, 0 = black and white.
tintcolor"#ffffff"Multiplied into the colours (white = none).

Looks: how entities appear

How an AR entity appears and disappears (content schema 2.29, put_experience_appearance): experience.appearance { reveal?, found?, lost? }, each a look { type, …params } like a pass – reveal = the first find of a target (the entry is unlocked with it), found = every later find, lost = the target is lost (its look plays rewound, in the look's outDuration). A moment without a look takes found's, and without that inflateDissolve; an experience without appearance plays inflateDissolve everywhere. The built-in looks share one set of parameters and differ in their defaults (builtIn: each look's params with its defaults); write only the values that differ. A look a plugin of the experience registers (api.registerAppearance, plugin API 1.8) is named the same way, its parameters checked against the recorded spec; the publish refuses a look no compiled plugin provides (409 unknown-appearances). An app before 2.29 ignores the field and plays its own animation.

momentsreveal · found · lost
defaultinflateDissolve

inflateDissolve builtIn

Flat and small on the page, the entity rises, grows and turns half around under a noise dissolve with a gold edge and sparks.

ParameterKindDefaultWhat
durationnumber · 50 … 10000 · in ms · step 103470How long it takes to appear. (shown as “appear”)
outDurationnumber · 50 … 10000 · in ms · step 10600How long it takes to disappear: the same animation, rewound. (shown as “disappear”)
maskchoice · "none" | "noise""noise"noise = a front moves through 3D noise and what it has not reached is not drawn yet (the dissolve); none = everything is drawn.
maskStartnumber · 0 … 1 · step 0.010Share of the time at which the front starts. (shown as “mask start”)
maskEndnumber · 0 … 1 · step 0.010.75Share of the time at which the front has passed everything. (shown as “mask end”)
wavesnumber · 0.5 … 12 · step 0.13Noise waves across the object.
edgeStartnumber · 0 … 0.5 · step 0.0050.06Width of the coloured edge at the front when it starts (0 = none). (shown as “edge from”)
edgeEndnumber · 0 … 0.5 · step 0.0050.015Width of the edge when the front has passed. (shown as “edge to”)
edgeColorcolor"#f3cc94"The edge's colour. (shown as “edge colour”)
edgeIntensitynumber · 0 … 4 · step 0.050.6Multiplies the edge's colour; above 1 it is brighter than white and blooms. (shown as “edge intensity”)
glownumber · 0 … 1 · step 0.010.6How strongly the band behind the edge shines in the glow colour (0 = none).
glowWidthnumber · 0 … 1 · step 0.010.2Width of the shining band behind the edge. (shown as “glow width”)
glowColorcolor"#f3cc94"The glow's colour. (shown as “glow colour”)
heightFromnumber · 0 … 1 · step 0.010Height along the page normal at the start, as a share of the real one: 0 = flat on the page (the inflate), 1 = unchanged. (shown as “height from”)
scaleFromnumber · 0 … 2 · step 0.010Size at the start, as a share of the real one (1 = unchanged). (shown as “scale from”)
spinnumber · -2 … 2 · in turns · step 0.05-0.5Turns around the page normal on the way in.

Environment

The experience's world around the reader while scanning and the onion sky (put_environment): { world, onionSky, worldSrc?, skySrc? } – worldSrc a glTF model (origin = the floor under the reader, +y up, −z towards the book), skySrc an equirectangular image (2:1): an uploaded asset's url or a /assets/content/… path. null = the default.

worldscafe
worldSrcExtensions.glb · .gltf
skySrcExtensions.jpg · .jpeg · .png · .webp

default

worldcafe
onionSkytrue

Pictures

The image rule (#298): every picture takes the same way into the experience. An uploaded jpg / png / webp is stored as WebP (quality 82; lossless when it has transparency – an icon, a cut-out), turned upright by its EXIF orientation, its metadata dropped, never scaled up, its longest side at most 2048 px for a surface's reference image and an entry's colour picture, 1200 px for a target's printed image and 2048 px for every other Library picture; a picture above 50 MP is refused (413 image-too-large). The upload does not know the use: upload_asset takes fit: "target" for a target's printed image and fit: "reference" (with scene and surface) for a surface's reference image. The stored file is named <name>.webp. TIFF and PDF are no Library files – convert them locally first (Pillow / PyMuPDF), then upload.

Subtitles

A video's subtitles (content schema 2.31): no field of a node. Upload a WebVTT file named <video name>.<language>.vtt with upload_asset – speak.en.vtt, speak.fr.vtt for speak.mp4 – and it belongs to every video of that name in the experience, uploaded or imported; the draft's configuration lists the files per video in subtitles. One file per language (en, de, fr, nl, pt-BR …), each cue 00:00:01.000 --> 00:00:03.500 and its text below, the times the video's own. The reader shows the line of its language while the video plays (else English, else the first), the editor's stage the English one.

Credits

Picture credits (content schema 2.33, #292): no field of an entry or a node. A file's credit line (one free text line – "Book Golem by TER-JAN / DeviantArt") is set in the Library with set_asset_credits and listed by list_assets; the experience's configuration carries the lines of the files it uses (credits: { <file URL>: <line> }), and the reader lists them per scene on its image credits page (Info → here).

Plugins

A plugin (the Code tab) is a folder of files (#352): index.ts exports register(api), TypeScript files next to it are imported by ./name, shader files (.frag, .vert, .glsl, .wgsl) as strings (import WATER from "./water.frag") – put_plugin takes them all. api.registerLayer(type, spec, { glsl }) for a material layer, api.registerComponent(type, spec, apply) for code on a node, api.registerNodeType(type, spec, build) for a node type of its own, api.registerMaterial(type, spec, build) for a whole material (a ShaderMaterial …, plugin API 1.4), api.registerTexture(type, spec, draw) for a procedural texture, api.feedback({ width, height, fragment }) for a GPU feedback buffer the engine steps every frame and api.shadertoy(source) for a Shadertoy pass as its fragment (plugin API 1.6, in a build – nothing of it is recorded), api.three for three.js – never import three. The spec's params have kind (number | color | choice | boolean | string | texture | model), default, description and an optional label (the few words the editor's row shows, plugin API 1.3); nodeTypes narrows the node types. A parameter of kind model (plugin API 1.7, content schema 2.28) takes a model file – an uploaded glb / gltf asset's url or a /assets/content/… path, "" = none – which the plugin's code loads with api.loadModel(value). Plugin API 3.1 (content schema 5.1): api.p builds the params (p.number({ min, max, slider? }), p.integer, p.boolean, p.string, p.choice([…]), p.color, p.texture, p.model, p.file(kind)) and the handler's params are typed from them; min / max are hard limits, slider the soft range; a spec may declare actions (rule verbs it answers: play, pause, stop, show, hide – onAction), events (scene events it emits through its context's emit) and uses ({ listens, emits, reads, sets } – the Logic view's joins; plugin API 4.0, content schema 6.0: listens was hears). Read the resource osct://guides/plugins.

idPattern^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$

Onboarding

The onboarding (the splash and the steps before the scan) is the reader app's own UI, translated with the app – no experience content and no tool edits it. The splash shows the experience's title and its printed book's author and publisher (update_experience).
